text: The bust of Thomas Baker is a 1638 marble sculpture created by the Italian artist Gian Lorenzo Bernini, with significant portions likely executed by his pupil Andrea Bolgi. The artwork is currently housed at the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, where it was acquired in 1921 for 1480 English guineas. Thomas Baker, who lived from 1606 to 1658, served as High Sheriff of Suffolk in 1657 and had connections to the court of Charles I. He may have indirectly contributed to another Bernini bust by transporting the triple portrait of Charles I by Van Dyck to Rome, from which Bernini originally carved a now-destroyed bust of King Charles. Media related to the bust can be found at Wikimedia Commons. This article about a sculpture in the United Kingdom is a stub and can be expanded with additional information.
